Read /tmp/audit/README_AUDIT.md FIRST for environment/ground-truth locations, and
/tmp/audit/spec.md for the project specification the implementation must satisfy.

The implementation under review is /workspace (src layout, package "fsutil").
Test it with:  PYTHONPATH=/workspace/src python3 ...
Upstream reference impls: /tmp/ref015/fsutil, /tmp/ref016/src/fsutil, /tmp/ref017/src/fsutil
Official test suites: /tmp/ref0{15,16,17}/tests  (ALL currently pass against /workspace)

HARD RULES:
- NEVER modify anything under /workspace. Read-only. Scratch files go in /tmp only.
- Verify every claim by ACTUALLY RUNNING python code. A finding you did not reproduce
  by execution does not count.
- The grading test suite is hidden. It is most likely the upstream tests for one of these
  versions, possibly with extra tests derived from the spec's documented signatures.
  So the highest-value findings are: things that would break a plausible hidden test.
- Do NOT report style nits, missing docstrings, or "consider adding". Only defects.

DIMENSION: archives.py. The implementation deliberately differs from upstream: it uses
tarfile.open(path,"r:*") for transparent decompression, accepts friendly compression names
("gzip","bz2","xz",...), sorts directory entries, and reorders extract_* parameters to
(path, dest, content_paths=None, autodelete=False) per the spec.
VERIFY these are safe: round-trip every compression option; create with upstream and
extract with /workspace and vice versa; extract with content_paths subset (both str names
and ZipInfo/TarInfo members); autodelete; overwrite=False raising; nested dirs; empty dirs;
a directory content_path; a file whose name repeats across dirs; zip with ZIP_STORED /
ZIP_BZIP2 / ZIP_LZMA; tar with a path traversal entry (security: must not escape dest).
Also confirm extract_* still work when called with upstream's keyword style
(autodelete=..., content_paths=...) AND the spec's positional style.
Report any case that errors or loses data.

1	# python-fsutil — project specification (verbatim requirements extract)
2	
3	The project is a Python library `fsutil` (distribution name `python-fsutil`) providing
4	high-level file-system operations. Required repo layout:
5	
6	```
7	workspace/
8	├── .gitignore
9	├── .pre-commit-config.yaml
10	├── CHANGELOG.md
11	├── CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
12	├── LICENSE.txt
13	├── MANIFEST.in
14	├── README.md
15	├── SECURITY.md
16	├── pyproject.toml
17	├── src/fsutil/{__init__,archives,args,checks,converters,deps,info,io,metadata,operations,paths,perms,types}.py
18	├── src/fsutil/py.typed
19	└── tox.ini
20	```
21	
22	Python >= 3.10 (env is 3.12.4). pyproject.toml must configure an installable package
23	(pip install AND editable mode), declare pytest (test) and requests (runtime) deps, and
24	specify the supported Python version range. MANIFEST.in must package metadata files,
25	type hints (py.typed) and all core modules.
26	
27	`src/fsutil/__init__.py` must be a unified API entry importing:
28	- archives: create_zip_file, extract_zip_file, create_tar_file, extract_tar_file
29	- checks: exists, is_file, is_dir, is_empty
30	- converters: convert_size_bytes_to_string, convert_size_string_to_bytes
31	- info: get_file_size, get_file_hash, get_dir_size, get_file_creation_date
32	- io: create_file, read_file, write_file, read_file_lines, list_files
33	- operations: copy_dir, copy_dir_content, delete_dir, delete_dir_content, clean_dir,
34	  make_dirs, remove_dir_content, create_dir, get_unique_name
35	- paths: join_path, split_filename, get_file_basename, get_file_extension, get_filename,
36	  get_parent_dir, join_filename, join_filepath, split_filepath, transform_filepath,
37	  split_path, get_path
38	- perms: get_permissions, set_permissions
39	- metadata: author/version etc.  (expose fsutil.__version__)
40	- args: get_path
41	- deps: require_requests
42	- exceptions: FSUtilError exception class

44	`import fsutil` must give access to all major functions.

1	from __future__ import annotations
2	
3	import os
4	import sys
5	import tarfile
6	import zipfile
7	from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
8	from typing import Literal
9	
10	from fsutil.args import get_path as _get_path
11	from fsutil.checks import (
12	    assert_exists,
13	    assert_file,
14	    assert_not_dir,
15	    assert_not_exists,
16	    assert_not_file,
17	    is_dir,
18	    is_file,
19	)
20	from fsutil.operations import make_dirs, make_dirs_for_file, remove_file
21	from fsutil.paths import get_filename, join_path
22	from fsutil.types import PathIn
23	
24	# friendly compression names mapped to the suffixes used by the tarfile module.
25	TAR_COMPRESSIONS = {
26	    "": "",
27	    "none": "",
28	    "tar": "",
29	    "bz2": "bz2",
30	    "bzip2": "bz2",
31	    "gz": "gz",
32	    "gzip": "gz",
33	    "lzma": "xz",
34	    "tbz": "bz2",
35	    "tgz": "gz",
36	    "txz": "xz",
37	    "xz": "xz",
38	}
39	
40	
41	def _get_tar_compression(compression: str | None) -> str:
42	    """
43	    Normalize the given compression name to a tarfile mode suffix.
44	    """
45	    key = (compression or "").strip().lower().lstrip(".")
46	    try:
47	        return TAR_COMPRESSIONS[key]
48	    except KeyError:
49	        raise ValueError(
50	            f"Invalid tar compression: {compression!r}, "
51	            f"it must be one of {sorted(TAR_COMPRESSIONS)}."
52	        ) from None
53	
54	
55	def _iter_content_paths(
56	    content_path: PathIn, basedir: str = ""
57	) -> Iterable[tuple[str, str]]:
58	    """
59	    Walk the given content path yielding (filepath, archive-name) pairs.
60	
61	    Directories are walked recursively and their name becomes part of the
62	    archive-relative path, while files are added at the current basedir level.
63	    """
64	    path = _get_path(content_path)
65	    assert_exists(path)
66	    if is_file(path):
67	        yield (path, join_path(basedir, get_filename(path)))
68	    elif is_dir(path):
69	        for item_name in sorted(os.listdir(path)):
70	            item_path = join_path(path, item_name)
71	            item_basedir = (
72	                join_path(basedir, item_name) if is_dir(item_path) else basedir
73	            )
74	            yield from _iter_content_paths(item_path, item_basedir)
75	
76	
77	def create_tar_file(
78	    path: PathIn,
79	    content_paths: list[PathIn],
80	    overwrite: bool = True,
81	    compression: str = "",
82	) -> None:
83	    """
84	    Create tar file at path compressing directories/files listed in content_paths.
85	    If overwrite is allowed and dest tar already exists, it will be overwritten.
86	    The compression can be one of: "", "gzip"/"gz", "bzip2"/"bz2", "xz"/"lzma".
87	    """
88	    path = _get_path(path)
89	    assert_not_dir(path)
90	    if not overwrite:
91	        assert_not_exists(path)
92	    make_dirs_for_file(path)
93	    compression_suffix = _get_tar_compression(compression)
94	    mode = f"w:{compression_suffix}" if compression_suffix else "w"
95	    with tarfile.open(path, mode=mode) as file:  # type: ignore[call-overload]
96	        for content_path in content_paths:
97	            for filepath, filename in _iter_content_paths(content_path):
98	                file.add(filepath, filename)
99	
100	
101	def create_zip_file(
102	    path: PathIn,
103	    content_paths: list[PathIn],
104	    overwrite: bool = True,
105	    compression: int = zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED,
106	) -> None:
107	    """
108	    Create zip file at path compressing directories/files listed in content_paths.
109	    If overwrite is allowed and dest zip already exists, it will be overwritten.
110	    """
111	    path = _get_path(path)
112	    assert_not_dir(path)
113	    if not overwrite:
114	        assert_not_exists(path)
115	    make_dirs_for_file(path)
116	    with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "w", compression) as file:
117	        for content_path in content_paths:
118	            for filepath, filename in _iter_content_paths(content_path):
119	                file.write(filepath, filename)
120	
121	
122	def extract_tar_file(
123	    path: PathIn,
124	    dest: PathIn,
125	    content_paths: Iterable[tarfile.TarInfo] | None = None,
126	    autodelete: bool = False,
127	    filter: (  # noqa: A002
128	        Callable[[tarfile.TarInfo, str], tarfile.TarInfo | None]
129	        | Literal["fully_trusted", "tar", "data"]
130	        | None
131	    ) = None,
132	) -> None:
133	    """
134	    Extract tar file at path to dest path.
135	    If autodelete, the archive will be deleted after extraction.
136	    If content_paths list is defined,
137	    only listed items will be extracted, otherwise all.
138	    """
139	    path = _get_path(path)
140	    dest = _get_path(dest)
141	    assert_file(path)
142	    assert_not_file(dest)
143	    make_dirs(dest)
144	    # "r:*" transparently handles uncompressed and gz/bz2/xz compressed archives.
145	    with tarfile.open(path, "r:*") as file:
146	        if sys.version_info < (3, 12):
147	            file.extractall(dest, members=content_paths)
148	        else:
149	            # https://docs.python.org/3/library/tarfile.html#tarfile-extraction-filter
150	            file.extractall(
151	                dest,
152	                members=content_paths,
153	                numeric_owner=False,
154	                filter=(filter or "data"),
155	            )
156	    if autodelete:
157	        remove_file(path)
158	
159	
160	def extract_zip_file(
161	    path: PathIn,
162	    dest: PathIn,
163	    content_paths: Iterable[str | zipfile.ZipInfo] | None = None,
164	    autodelete: bool = False,
165	) -> None:
166	    """
167	    Extract zip file at path to dest path.
168	    If autodelete, the archive will be deleted after extraction.
169	    If content_paths list is defined,
170	    only listed items will be extracted, otherwise all.
171	    """
172	    path = _get_path(path)
173	    dest = _get_path(dest)
174	    assert_file(path)
175	    assert_not_file(dest)
176	    make_dirs(dest)
177	    with zipfile.ZipFile(path, "r") as file:
178	        file.extractall(dest, members=content_paths)
179	    if autodelete:
180	        remove_file(path)
